mainTopic: Broken ovens and torn hides: when a broken item still counts as whole, and when flesh on a hide is cancelled
overview: The amud opens with an objection to ריש לקיש, who holds that a broken item still held together counts as one piece. The objection uses a משנה about purifying a טמא oven. רבא answers by rereading the משנה: everyone agrees a טמא oven must be divided into three and have its plaster scraped off. רבי מאיר is lenient only about keeping an oven from ever becoming טמא. Next the גמרא sets 'divide it into three' against another משנה that measures a broken oven's leftovers by four טפחים, and resolves the clash by the way the oven was cut. It then settles how small 'any size' is and which oven sizes go with each measure. Next comes a dispute between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן about whether a scarf-sized piece of a torn hide still counts. Finally a new משנה teaches when flesh on a נבלה hide makes a person טמא. The גמרא follows a long story about where רבי יוחנן's rule (flesh cut loose with a knife is cancelled) belongs, and its answer, built on a teaching of רב פפא, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the oven משנה: רבי מאיר's easier method
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה finishes. The רבנן require scraping off the plaster until the oven rests on the ground. רבי מאיר says it is enough to cut the oven down from inside to less than four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: …until it rests on the ground. רבי מאיר says: You don't need to scrape off the plaster, and certainly not all the way down to the ground. Instead, you cut the oven down from the inside until it is less than four handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a משנה about how to make a טמא oven טהור. This quote sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say the oven only becomes טהור if its plaster is scraped away, so that nothing holds it together. רבי מאיר says you can leave the plaster in place, as long as you shrink the oven to under four טפחים. That means the oven becomes טהור even though the plaster still holds the pieces together.

keyTerms.meaning: The plaster or clay coating around the outside of the oven that holds it in place
To scrape off
He reduces it, makes it smaller
Handbreadths, a unit of measure

phrases.english: until it rests on the ground.
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לֹא לִגְרוֹר אֶת הַטְּפֵילָה
phrases.english: One does not need to scrape off the plaster,
and certainly not until it rests on the ground;
rather, he reduces it from within
to less than four handbreadths.
phrases.notes: Some versions read the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the one in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לֹא לִגְרוֹר אֶת הַטְּפֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה that the objection against ריש לקיש is built on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: shrinking the oven to under four טפחים from inside is enough to make it טהור, without removing the plaster.

steps.title: Why is the oven טהור if the plaster still holds it together?
steps.stepSummary: The objection against ריש לקיש: according to רבי מאיר the shrunken oven is טהור. But the plaster still holds it together, so ריש לקיש should say it is still one connected, טמא oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once he cuts it down to less than four, at least, it is טהור. Why? Say that it is held together and standing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש using רבי מאיר's ruling. If a broken item that is held together still counts as whole, this oven should still be טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule says a broken item that is still held together (חלים וקאי) is treated as connected. Under רבי מאיר, the plaster still holds the cut oven together, and yet it is טהור. That seems to go against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: At least, in any event
Why?
It is whole and standing, meaning it is held together as if repaired

phrases.english: When he reduces it to less than four,
at least it is pure. Why?
Let us say: it is held together and standing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי מאיר's ruling from the משנה to attack ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a broken item held together (חלים וקאי) counts as connected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי מאיר, the oven is טהור even though the plaster still holds it together. That suggests being held together does not make it count as whole.

steps.title: רבא: You could bring support from the רבנן instead
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back on the objection. Why use רבי מאיר against ריש לקיש? The רבנן require scraping the plaster all the way to the ground, and that supports ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Then say it from the רבנן: one scrapes off the plaster until it rests on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the objection. He points out that the other opinion in the same משנה, the רבנן's, actually backs up ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say the oven is not טהור until the plaster is scraped away, so that nothing holds the pieces together. That fits ריש לקיש exactly: as long as it is held together, it still counts as whole. So the משנה is not clearly against ריש לקיש, and at most the issue depends on which opinion you follow.

keyTerms.meaning: And say instead, why not say
Here: from the view of the רבנן, the sages who disagree with רבי מאיר

steps.confusionAlert: מדרבנן here does NOT mean 'rabbinic law' as opposed to Torah law. It means 'from the opinion of the רבנן' in this משנה, the ones who disagree with רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But say it from the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹרֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵילָה עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: one scrapes off the plaster until it rests on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the challenge in step 2 by pointing to the other opinion in the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the משנה clearly disproves ריש לקיש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge chose רבי מאיר and ignored the רבנן, whose opinion supports ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רבא rereads the משנה: everyone agrees on the basic method
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a better reading of the משנה. Everyone, even רבי מאיר, agrees that a טמא oven is purified by dividing it into three and scraping the plaster down to the ground. That fits ריש לקיש for all opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what the משנה means. How do you purify a טמא oven? Everyone agrees: you divide it into three, and scrape off the plaster until it rests on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back his first answer and offers a new reading of the משנה. In this reading, everyone agrees on the basic method of purifying the oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, it looked as if רבי מאיר disagreed with ריש לקיש. Now רבא says the basic method, splitting the oven and removing the plaster, is accepted by everyone. That means even רבי מאיר holds that an oven held together by plaster is still whole. The גמרא will go on to explain what the argument with רבי מאיר is actually about.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; a rereading of a text
Everyone agrees
He divides it into three pieces
Oven

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא's final reading, nobody holds that an oven held together by its plaster is already broken. So the משנה is no challenge to ריש לקיש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rescues ריש לקיש's rule of חלים וקאי. It shows that even the more lenient opinion, רבי מאיר's, agrees that pieces held together still count as one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: This is what it is saying:
An oven that became impure, how does one purify it?
Everyone agrees: one divides it into three,

phrases.aramaic: וְגוֹרֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵילָה עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בָּאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: and scrapes off the plaster until it rests on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's first answer with a full rereading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה so that the basic method is agreed by everyone
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר seemed to hold that an oven held together by plaster can be טהור, which goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone, including רבי מאיר, requires dividing the oven and scraping off the plaster, so ריש לקיש's rule stands for all opinions.

steps.title: How to make an oven that never becomes טמא
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rereading goes on: the argument between the רבנן and רבי מאיר is only about preventing an oven from becoming טמא. The רבנן say even then you divide it into three and scrape the plaster to the ground. רבי מאיר says it is enough to cut the oven down from the inside to less than four טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone wants his oven never to become טמא, what does he do? He divides it into three parts and scrapes off the plaster until the oven sits on the ground. רבי מאיר says: he does not need to scrape off the plaster, and it does not need to reach the ground. He just makes the oven smaller from the inside, to less than four טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his rereading of the משנה. He places the disagreement of רבי מאיר and the רבנן in a different case: an oven that is not yet טמא, whose owner wants to keep it from ever becoming טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By moving רבי מאיר's leniency to an oven that is still טהור, רבא removes the challenge to ריש לקיש. רבי מאיר never says that a טמא oven held together by plaster becomes טהור. He only says that an oven cut below four טפחים before becoming טמא can never become טמא, while the רבנן treat prevention like purification.

keyTerms.meaning: into a state of טומאה, meaning able to become טמא
the outer layer of plaster or clay smeared around the oven
scrapes off
reduces it from the inside, making the oven itself smaller

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי מאיר is talking about an oven that is NOT yet טמא. Do not mix this up with how to purify an oven that is already טמא. Step 4 showed that everyone agrees that case needs dividing into three and scraping.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא תַּנּוּרוֹ לִידֵי טוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: And one who wants his oven not to come to impurity,
how does he act?
He divides it into three,
and scrapes off the plaster
until it is on the ground.
Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לֹא לִגְרוֹר אֶת הַטְּפֵילָה
phrases.english: He does not need to scrape off the plaster
and not until it is on the ground,
rather, he reduces it from inside
to less than four handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָרוֹצֶה שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא תַּנּוּרוֹ לִידֵי טוּמְאָה, כֵּיצַד הוּא עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's rereading begun in step 4: everyone agrees about purification, and the dispute is only about prevention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: to prevent טומאה, divide into three and scrape the plaster to the ground. רבי מאיר: it is enough to reduce the inside below four טפחים.

steps.title: Zooming in on 'divides it into three'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks out one phrase from the משנה, 'he divides it into three,' so it can examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He divides it into three.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes one phrase from the משנה to get ready for its next move, a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dividing into three makes sure that no single piece holds most of the oven. The גמרא is about to ask whether this fits with another משנה about how big leftover oven pieces must be to stay טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: he divides it, splitting the oven into pieces
into three parts

phrases.english: The Master said: He divides it into three.
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here just means the משנה that was quoted. The גמרא is picking out this one phrase to look at.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה as a whole to one specific phrase in it, getting ready for a contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the rule that an oven is divided into three.

steps.title: A contradiction from the משנה about oven sizes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another משנה. רבי מאיר there says a new oven needs four טפחים to be able to become טמא, and leftover pieces of four טפחים stay טמא. The חכמים say this applies only to a large oven. A small oven can become טמא at any size, and its leftovers stay טמא if they hold most of the oven. This seems to clash with the simple rule of 'divide it into three.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא sets a contradiction against it: An oven, at its start, needs four טפחים, and its leftovers need four טפחים. These are the words of רבי מאיר. And the חכמים say: When was this said? About a large oven. But a small oven, at its start, is any size, once its building is finished. And its leftovers stay טמא if they are most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different משנה that seems to clash with 'divide it into three.' It is setting up a problem that it will spell out and answer next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first משנה, the רבנן require dividing the oven into three, so that no single piece holds most of the oven. That implies a piece holding most of the oven keeps it טמא. In this משנה the חכמים seem to accept רבי מאיר's four-טפחים measure for a large oven, which implies that size, not 'most of the oven,' decides. Step 10 spells out this clash.

keyTerms.meaning: and the גמרא raises a contradiction, setting one source against another
its start, meaning when the oven is first finished
its leftovers, the broken pieces that remain
in what case was this said, a phrase that limits a rule
any size at all
with most of it, holding the majority of the oven

steps.confusionAlert: 'Its start' is about when an oven first becomes able to be טמא. 'Its leftovers' is about the broken pieces of an oven that was already טמא. These are two separate rules.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
An oven, its start is four,
phrases.notes: A new oven can become טמא only once it is four טפחים tall.

phrases.english: and its leftovers are four,
phrases.notes: If a טמא oven breaks, a remaining piece four טפחים tall stays טמא.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
In what case was this said?
In a large one,
but in a small one, its start is any size,
once its making is finished,
its leftovers are with its majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the phrase quoted in step 6 and sets it against a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that dividing an oven into three is enough (חולקו לשלשה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים here seem to accept four טפחים as the measure for a large oven's leftovers. That implies a piece under four טפחים is טהור even if it is most of the oven. But 'divide into three' assumes a piece holding most of the oven stays טמא.

steps.title: How small is 'any size'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חכמים meant when they said a small oven can become טמא at 'any size.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'any size'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about one phrase from the משנה it just quoted: 'any size' for a small oven. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, 'any size' would mean even a tiny oven. But an oven has to be usable to count as a real כלי. So the גמרא wants an actual smallest size.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much? (asking for an exact size)
Any size at all, even the smallest amount
A small oven, the case the חכמים were talking about

phrases.english: And how much is 'any size'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what one phrase means in the משנה quoted in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The smallest real size of a small oven that can become טמא.

steps.title: One handbreadth, because people make ovens that small
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי says 'any size' means one טפח, since people really do make ovens one טפח tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי says: one טפח, because people make ovens one טפח tall.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ינאי answers the question. 'Any size' means one טפח, because ovens that small really exist and get used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size is based on real life. Since people actually make one-טפח ovens, an oven that small is a real כלי and can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a unit of measure about the width of a hand
Literally 'daughters of a טפח,' meaning ovens one טפח in size
Because, since (gives the reason)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai says: one handbreadth,
since people make ovens one handbreadth tall.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets uses a slightly different form of 'ovens.' The meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Any size' means one טפח, the size of ovens people actually make.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one-טפח size becomes the basis for the question in Step 12.

steps.title: The רבנן seem to need four handbreadths for leftover pieces
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה in כלים, the גמרא infers that the רבנן agree a large oven's leftovers stay טמא only if a piece is four טפחים. That clashes with 'divide it into three,' which goes by whether a piece is most of the oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason it stays טמא is that its leftovers are four טפחים. That means if its leftovers are not four טפחים, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a careful inference from the משנה in כלים and uses it to raise a contradiction. For a large oven, the leftovers seem to stay טמא only when a piece is four טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים limited רבי מאיר's four-טפחים rule to a large oven, they seem to accept it there. So a broken large oven with no four-טפח piece would be טהור, even if one piece is most of the oven. But the 'divide it into three' rule means one piece holding most of the oven keeps it טמא. Those two rules seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason (the גמרא is pointing to exactly why the law is so)
But this means (introduces the opposite case)
Its leftovers, the broken pieces of the oven
Pure, not able to pass on טומאה

phrases.english: The reason is because its leftovers are four handbreadths,
but if its leftovers are not four handbreadths, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא שְׁיָרָיו אַרְבַּע, הָא לֵיכָּא שְׁיָרָיו אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the large-oven part of the משנה from Step 7 and draws an inference that clashes with the 'divide it into three' rule from Steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'divide it into three' rule of the רבנן, which goes by whether a piece is most of the oven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the four-טפחים size decides it, a large oven with no four-טפח piece is טהור even if one piece is most of the oven. But dividing into three only matters if a piece holding most of the oven would keep it טמא.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different measures here. One is size, four טפחים. The other is a share, most of the oven. The clash is about which one decides whether the leftovers stay טמא.

steps.title: Two different ways of cutting the oven
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the four-טפחים משנה is about an oven cut across into rings. The 'divide it into three' משנה is about an oven split down its length into standing shards.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: There, he cut it across. Here, he made it into a shard (split down its length).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 10. It shows the two משניות are talking about different ways of breaking the oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the oven is cut across into rings, the pieces cannot stand stably on each other. So only a piece of four טפחים is still a real oven. When the oven is split down its length into shards, a piece that holds most of the oven can still stand and work. So that is why 'most of the oven' is what matters there.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the other source)
Here (the source we are learning now)
He cut it across, splitting the oven sideways into rings
A shard, a lengthwise piece of the oven that can still stand

steps.whatToRemember: How the oven was broken decides the measure. If it was cut across, a piece needs four טפחים. If it was split lengthwise into shards, the question is whether one piece is most of the oven.

phrases.english: They said: There, it is where he cut it across;
phrases.notes: 'There' is the משנה that needs four טפחים. The pieces are rings that cannot stand steadily on top of each other.

phrases.english: here, it is where he made it into a shard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם, דְּצַלְקֵיהּ מִצְלָק; הָכָא, דְּעַבְדֵיהּ גִּיסְטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in Step 10 by giving each משנה a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: each source is about a different way of cutting the oven.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to be about the same broken oven, so their rules seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cut across into rings, a piece needs four טפחים. Split lengthwise into shards, a piece needs to be most of the oven.

steps.title: What use is most of one handbreadth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the small oven. If a small oven can be one טפח, its leftovers might be only most of a טפח. A piece that small seems useless, so why should it stay טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: its leftovers stay טמא if they are most of it. But what use is most of a טפח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the small-oven rule again and raises a new difficulty. It combines that rule with the one-טפח size given by the school of רבי ינאי in Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small oven's leftovers stay טמא if they hold most of the oven. A small oven can be as small as one טפח. So a leftover piece could be only most of a טפח. Something must be usable to keep its טומאה, and a piece that tiny seems to have no use.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of it, the majority
What is it good for? What use is it?
Impure, able to pass on טומאה

phrases.english: The Master said: its leftovers are impure if they are most of it,
but what use is most of a handbreadth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: שְׁיָרָיו בְּרוּבּוֹ, רוּבּוֹ דְּטֶפַח לְמַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new difficulty by combining the small-oven rule from Step 7 with the one-טפח size from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's rule that a small oven's leftovers stay טמא if they hold most of the oven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole oven can be one טפח, most of it is less than a טפח. A piece that small has no use, so it should not stay טמא.

steps.title: אביי: the 'most of it' rule is about a large oven
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the question about the tiny oven. The 'leftovers by most' rule is said about a large oven, not a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The leftovers of a large oven stay impure if they are most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 12. He says the rule 'leftovers stay טמא if they are most of the oven' was never about a small oven. It was about a large oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that most of a one-טפח oven is a useless crumb. אביי moves the 'most of it' rule over to the large oven, where most of the oven is a real, usable piece. So the question about the tiny leftover goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: the leftovers or remains (of a broken utensil)
the large (oven)
by its majority, meaning the piece must be most of the whole

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The leftovers of a large one are by its majority,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12 about the useless leftover of a one-טפח oven.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the rule to a different case: 'most of it' is said about a large oven, not a small one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'most of it' was about the small oven, which left a useless crumb.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Most of it' is about a large oven, so the leftover is a sizable piece.

steps.title: But the Rabbis said four טפחים for a large oven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the רבנן said a large oven's leftovers need four טפחים, so how can אביי say they need to be most of the oven?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Rabbis say four?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי. The רבנן already gave a measure for a large oven's leftovers, and that measure is four טפחים, not 'most of it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings back the clash from Step 10. If the large oven's measure is four טפחים, then putting the 'most of it' rule on the large oven gives two different measures for the same oven.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't they say? (opens a challenge)
four (טפחים)

phrases.english: But didn't the Rabbis say four?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a large oven's leftovers are measured by 'most of it.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן already set four טפחים as the measure for a large oven, so 'most of it' seems to contradict them.

steps.title: A nine-טפח oven and a seven-טפח oven
steps.stepSummary: No problem: one rule is about an oven nine טפחים tall, and the other is about an oven seven טפחים tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about a nine-handbreadth oven, and that one is about a seven-handbreadth oven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both rules are true. Each one is about a large oven of a different height.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Most of it' is said about a nine-טפח oven, and 'four טפחים' is said about a seven-טפח oven. Since the two rules are about different sizes of oven, they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (the answer comes next)
oven
nine (טפחים) tall
seven (טפחים) tall

steps.whatToRemember: Small ovens stay at the size from רבי ינאי's school (one טפח). For large ovens, 'most of it' goes with a nine-טפח oven, and 'four טפחים' goes with a seven-טפח oven.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is about an oven nine (handbreadths tall),
that is about an oven seven (handbreadths tall).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּתַנּוּרָא בַּר תִּשְׁעָה, הָא בְּתַנּוּרָא בַּר שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two rules between two different oven sizes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rules seemed to be about the same large oven and to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Most of it' is about a nine-טפח oven, and 'four טפחים' is about a seven-טפח oven.

steps.title: Another version: the torn garment is טהור even with a scarf-sized piece left
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second version of רב הונא's ruling about a torn טלית. Here, even if a piece the size of a scarf is left untorn, the garment becomes טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it in another way: רב הונא said in the name of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי: Even if he left in it the size of a scarf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier topic: a טמא garment that was torn through most of its length. It gives a different version of רב הונא's statement about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once most of a garment is torn, it is no longer one whole garment, so it becomes טהור. In this version, an untorn strip the size of a מעפורת (scarf) is not enough to keep it טמא. A strip that size does not count for much.

keyTerms.meaning: another version (of what was said)
he left over
a scarf or wrap; used here as a measure of size

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions up. This version says the garment is טהור even with a scarf-sized piece left untorn.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:
And even if he left in it the size of a scarf.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the טמא garment that was torn through most of its length. The words left unsaid are 'it is still טהור.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the oven discussion and returns to רב הונא's earlier ruling about a torn garment, giving a second version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once most of the garment is torn, it is טהור even if a scarf-sized piece is left untorn.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: this is only true of a garment, not a hide
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש limits the ruling to a טלית. A scarf-sized piece of hide is valued, so the hide stays טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: They taught this only about a garment. But a hide is valued.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש says the scarf-sized rule from Step 16 only applies to cloth. With leather (עור), the leftover piece still matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scarf-sized piece of cloth is not worth much, so it cannot keep the garment טמא. A piece of leather that size is worth something, so ריש לקיש says it keeps the hide טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only about (a limit on the rule)
a cloth garment
leather or hide
valued, counts as important

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
They taught this only about a garment,
but a hide is valued,

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא טַלִּית, אֲבָל עוֹר – חֲשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of Step 16 to cloth garments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scarf-sized piece of hide is valued, so a torn hide with such a piece left stays טמא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a hide is not valued
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. Even a scarf-sized piece of hide does not count, so the hide also becomes טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even a hide is also not valued.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with ריש לקיש. He says the rule from Step 16 covers leather too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, leather gets no special treatment. Once most of it is torn, a scarf-sized piece left untorn does not keep it טמא, just as with cloth.

keyTerms.meaning: is not valued, does not count

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even a hide is also not valued.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ עוֹר נָמֵי לָא חֲשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A torn hide also becomes טהור, even if a scarf-sized piece is left.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from a טמא hide planned for straps and sandals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes a משנה against ריש לקיש. A hide is טמא מדרס, and its owner plans to make straps and sandals from it. רבי יהודה says it becomes טהור as soon as he cuts it with a knife. The חכמים say it stays טמא until it is less than five טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised an objection to ריש לקיש: A hide that is impure with מדרס, and he planned to make straps and sandals from it: once he puts a knife to it, it is pure. These are the words of רבי יהודה. And the Sages say: Not until he makes it smaller than five handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a משנה to challenge ריש לקיש's view that a piece of hide still counts. This step quotes the source; the exact point of the attack comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about a hide that is טמא מדרס, the impurity from a זב treading or sitting on it. Its owner plans to cut it into small leather items. רבי יהודה says the first cut with a knife already makes it טהור, so the hide is not treated as an important whole once cutting starts. The חכמים require it to be cut down below five טפחים, which sets a measure for when a piece of hide stops counting.

keyTerms.meaning: impurity a זב gives to something by treading, sitting or lying on it
he intended or planned (to use it for something)
a leather strap
sandals
a knife or scalpel

steps.confusionAlert: This step only quotes the source. The גמרא has not yet said how this משנה goes against ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
A hide that is impure with מדרס,
and he planned to make it into straps and sandals,
once he puts a knife to it, it is pure,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
Not until he makes it smaller than five handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן brings a source against ריש לקיש's position from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that a remaining piece of hide is valued and keeps the hide טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives rules for when a טמא hide that is being cut up becomes טהור. The exact contradiction with ריש לקיש is spelled out after this step.

steps.title: Why does hide cut below five handbreadths become pure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן finishes his challenge. Even the חכמים agree that once the hide is cut below five טפחים it is טהור. According to ריש לקיש a small piece should be valued, so why?
steps.simpleTranslation: But at least when he cuts it down, everyone agrees it is pure. Why? Let us say it is valued!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now spells out the point of the משנה he quoted. Even the חכמים say the hide becomes טהור once it is under five טפחים, and that does not fit ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said a scarf-sized piece of hide is valued, so it stays טמא. If small pieces are valued, a piece under five טפחים should also stay טמא. But the חכמים say it becomes טהור, so it seems small pieces of hide are not valued.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts it down, makes it smaller (here: below five טפחים)
Counts as valuable or important
Ritually pure

phrases.english: But at least when he cuts it down, it is pure.
Why? Let us say it is valued!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְמַעֵט מִיהָא טָהוֹר, אַמַּאי? לֵימָא חֲשִׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that began with the משנה quoted in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that a scarf-sized piece of hide is valued and stays טמא (Step 17).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If small pieces of hide are valued, a piece under five טפחים should stay טמא. The משנה says it becomes טהור, so small pieces are not valued.

steps.title: The case is a hide meant as a seat for a זב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about someone who wants the hide as a seat for a זב. A piece under five טפחים cannot be used as a seat, so in that case it is not valued.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where he wants the hide for a seat for a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer, given for ריש לקיש, is that the משנה is about a special case: the hide was meant to be a seat for a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a piece is valued depends on what it is meant for. A small piece is too small to sit on, so for a seat it is worthless and becomes טהור. That does not show that small pieces of hide are worthless in general, so ריש לקיש's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" The גמרא is narrowing a source to a specific case.
A seat used by a זב, which becomes טמא מדרס
A man with a discharge that makes him טמא

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where he wants it for a seat for a zav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by narrowing the משנה to a specific use.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about hide meant as a seat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say that small pieces of hide are never valued.
steps.terutzMaskana: Small pieces are worthless only when the hide was meant as a seat. In general they can still be valued, as ריש לקיש said.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a small piece "counts" depends on what the owner wants it for. Too small for a seat means worthless for a seat.

steps.title: משנה: hide with an olive-size of flesh
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If a נבלה hide has a כזית of flesh on it, someone who touches a strand of that flesh, or a hair on the other side, becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A hide with a כזית of flesh on it: one who touches a strand coming out of the flesh, or a hair on the other side of it, is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that touching a strand of the flesh, or a hair on the opposite side of the hide, is like touching the flesh itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you become טמא by touching a כזית of נבלה flesh. Here you touched only a strand or a hair, yet you are still טמא. The strand and the hair are treated as part of the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's size, the smallest amount of נבלה that makes something טמא
A thin strand or fiber of flesh
A hair
Ritually impure

phrases.english: Mishnah
A hide with an olive-size of flesh on it:
one who touches a strand coming out of it
or a hair opposite it,
phrases.notes: The hair is on the outside of the hide, right behind where the flesh is.

phrases.english: is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching a strand of the flesh, or a hair opposite it, on a hide holding a כזית of נבלה flesh makes a person טמא.

steps.title: Two half olive-sizes: carrying versus touching
steps.stepSummary: If the hide has two half-כזיתים on it, רבי ישמעאל says it makes one טמא by carrying but not by touching. רבי עקיבא says it makes one טמא neither way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were two half-olive-sizes on it, it makes one טמא by carrying but not by touching, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: neither by touching nor by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a disagreement about a hide with two separate half-כזיתים of flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, lifting the hide lifts both halves together, so together they make a full כזית. Touching reaches only one half at a time, which is too little. רבי עקיבא says the halves never join, even when carried.

keyTerms.meaning: Halves of an olive-size
Carrying, a way of becoming טמא by lifting something
Touching, a way of becoming טמא by contact

phrases.english: If there were on it two half-olive-sizes,
it makes impure by carrying but not by touching:
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
neither by touching nor by carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a full כזית to two halves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: the two halves join for carrying but not for touching. רבי עקיבא: they do not join at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ways of becoming טמא. Carrying (מַשָּׂא) means lifting both halves at once. Touching (מַגָּע) means contact with one piece at a time.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees about halves on a wood chip
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא agrees that if someone stuck two half-כזיתים on a wood chip and moved them, he is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא agrees that if someone stuck two half-olive-sizes on a wood chip and moved them, he is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where even רבי עקיבא says the two halves join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a wood chip, moving the two halves together does join them into a כזית, even for רבי עקיבא. So his ruling for the hide is not a general rule that halves never join. Something about the hide must be different.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, admits to a case
A wood chip or splinter
Moved them (moving something, even without lifting it, can pass on טומאה)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees
about two half-olive-sizes
that he stuck on a wood chip and moved,
that he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי עקיבא's view from Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-כזיתים moved together on a wood chip join to make the person טמא, even according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why is the hide different?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: why does רבי עקיבא rule טהור when the halves are on a hide, if moving them together on a chip makes one טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does רבי עקיבא rule pure in the case of the hide?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up its explanation of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the hide also moves both halves together, just like the wood chip. So it is unclear why the hide case should be טהור. The next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules something pure

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר בָּעוֹר?
phrases.english: And for what reason does Rabbi Akiva rule pure with the hide?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר בָּעוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the gap between the hide case (Step 23) and the wood chip case (Step 24).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes the hide different from a wood chip in רבי עקיבא's view?

steps.title: The hide cancels out the flesh
steps.stepSummary: Because the hide cancels out the two small pieces of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the hide cancels them out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question: on a hide, the small bits of flesh are cancelled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wood chip is just something to hold the flesh, so the flesh stays itself. The hide is attached to the flesh and is the main thing, so two small half-pieces become part of it. Once they are part of the hide, they no longer count as flesh at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels them out, makes them lose their own identity (from בִּטּוּל)

phrases.english: Because the hide cancels them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hide cancels out the small pieces of flesh, which a wood chip does not do.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, small pieces of flesh on a hide are cancelled out by the hide. On a wood chip they are not, so they join and make one טמא.

steps.title: Only when an animal tore the flesh loose
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן: the משנה's rule that the flesh on the hide still counts applies only when an animal tore it loose. If a knife cut it loose, the flesh is cancelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They only taught this when an animal tore it loose. But if a knife cut it loose, it is cancelled out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי יוחנן limits the first rule of the משנה, that the flesh on the hide still counts as flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal bit the flesh loose, no person decided anything, so the flesh keeps its status. If a person cut it with a knife, his action shows he does not care about this flesh, so it is cancelled out into the hide. The משנה's rule therefore covers only the animal case.

keyTerms.meaning: "They only taught this in the case of..." A formula that limits a source.
Literally "spat it out": tore or cut it loose
A knife
Is cancelled out, loses its own status

phrases.english: Gemara
Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They only taught this when an animal tore it loose,
phrases.notes: "This" goes back to the first case of the משנה, where touching the flesh on the hide makes a person טמא.

phrases.english: but if a knife cut it loose,
it is cancelled out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by limiting the first rule of the משנה (Step 22).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flesh on a hide still counts as flesh only if an animal tore it loose. If a person cut it with a knife, it is cancelled out into the hide.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's own action can decide whether something is cancelled out (בטל). The rest of the גמרא builds on this idea.

steps.title: Does the rule apply even to huge pieces of flesh?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks עולא whether רבי יוחנן's rule applies even to a piece as big as a תרטא, and even one as big as a sifter. עולא says yes both times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן asked עולא: Did רבי יוחנן really say this even about a piece of flesh as big as a תרטא? עולא said: Yes. And even as big as a sifter? He said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tests how far עולא's report of רבי יוחנן's rule goes. Does knife-cut flesh get cancelled into the hide no matter how big it is?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 27, עולא said that knife-cut flesh on the hide is cancelled. רב נחמן pushes the rule to extreme sizes to see whether it really has no limit. עולא confirms that it has none, which sets up רב נחמן's strong reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measure, a quarter of a קַב
A sifter or sieve, meaning a very large piece
Yes

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Ulla:
Did Rabbi Yochanan say this even about a piece the size of a tarta?
phrases.notes: A תרטא is a big piece of meat, a quarter of a קב, not a tiny scrap.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
And even a piece the size of a sifter?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the scope of עולא's report in Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the knife-cut cancellation rule apply even to very large pieces of flesh?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. According to עולא, it applies even to a piece the size of a תרטא or a sifter.

steps.title: רב נחמן refuses to accept the rule
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן swears that even if רבי יוחנן told him this himself, he would not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: By God! Even if רבי יוחנן told me this from his own mouth, I would not listen to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן flatly rejects the rule as עולא reported it, using an oath to show how strongly he feels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רב נחמן, it makes no sense that a huge piece of meat would become cancelled into a hide just because a knife cut it loose. He is rejecting עולא's version of the rule, the one that has no size limit. He is not attacking רבי יוחנן's idea in general.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath: 'By God!'
From his own mouth
I would not listen to him

phrases.english: He said to him: By God!

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִפּוּמֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: Even if Rabbi Yochanan said it to me from his own mouth,
I would not listen to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: האלהים אם אמר לי רבי יוחנן מפומיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to עולא's 'yes' answers by rejecting the rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the rule as עולא reported it, where any amount of knife-cut flesh is cancelled.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes no sense for very large pieces of flesh to be cancelled into a hide.

steps.title: רב נחמן is criticized in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא tells רבי אמי what עולא said and how רב נחמן answered. The reply is sharp: can רב נחמן belittle רבי יוחנן's teaching just because he married into the נשיא's family?
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב אושעיא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי אמי and told him the teaching: this is what עולא said, and this is how רב נחמן answered him. He said to him: Just because רב נחמן is the son-in-law of the נשיא's family, can he belittle רבי יוחנן's teaching?!
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to ארץ ישראל, where רב נחמן's harsh rejection of רבי יוחנן's teaching is criticized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The criticism takes for granted that עולא reported רבי יוחנן correctly, so רב נחמן seems to be disrespecting a great teacher. This is a challenge to רב נחמן's reaction. The next steps will show that the real problem was where the rule had been placed in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, here meaning from בבל to ארץ ישראל
A teaching or halachic statement
Son-in-law of the family of the נשיא
Belittles, treats lightly

phrases.english: When Rav Oshaya went up,
he found Rabbi Ami,
and he said the teaching in front of him:
This is what Ulla said,
and this is how Rav Nachman answered him.
He said to him: And just because Rav Nachman
is the son-in-law of the Nasi's family,
can he belittle the teaching of Rabbi Yochanan?!

steps.triggerLanguage: ומשום דרב נחמן חתניה דבי נשיאה הוא מזלזל בשמעתיה דרבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes רב נחמן's rejection in Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's refusal to accept רבי יוחנן's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוחנן said it, רב נחמן's social standing gives him no right to dismiss it.

steps.title: רבי אמי teaches the rule on the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Another time, רב אושעיא found רבי אמי applying the teaching to the סיפא: the case of two half-כזיתים, where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, he found him sitting and saying it on the last part of the משנה: If there were two half-כזיתים on it, they make one טמא by carrying but not by touching. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: neither by touching nor by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: This sets up the next move. The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's rule was actually taught on a different part of the משנה, the case of two half-כזיתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא quotes the סיפא again here on purpose, to show where רבי יוחנן's statement really belongs. That case is about small pieces of flesh, not one large piece. So the question of huge pieces never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
At another time
Halves of an olive-size (half-כזיתים)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a repeat of Step 23. The משנה is quoted again to show that רבי יוחנן's rule belongs here, not on the earlier case.

phrases.english: Another time he found him
sitting and saying it about the last part of the Mishnah:
If there were two half-olive-sizes on it,
they make one impure by carrying but not by touching;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
neither by touching nor by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: זמנין אשכחיה דיתיב וקאמר לה אסיפא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves רבי יוחנן's teaching to the סיפא, setting up the answer to רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's statement is about the case of two half-כזיתים on the hide.

steps.title: רבי אמי's version: knife-cut half-כזיתים are cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement belongs to רבי ישמעאל's ruling. The two halves make one טמא by carrying only when an animal tore them loose. If a knife cut them loose, they are cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They taught this only when an animal tore the flesh loose. But if a knife cut it loose, it is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי יוחנן's statement as רבי אמי taught it, on the case of the small half-כזיתים. In this version, רב נחמן's objection about huge pieces would not come up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small bits of flesh cut loose by a knife can easily become cancelled into the hide. That is very different from a huge piece the size of a תרטא or a sifter. Once the rule is placed on the סיפא, רב נחמן had no reason to object.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a specific case
Tore it loose or cut it loose
Is cancelled, becomes part of the hide

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי אמי's version, רבי יוחנן's knife-versus-animal rule is about two half-כזיתים, small pieces, so רב נחמן's objection would not arise. Step 36 shows that others taught it on the רישא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much depends on which part of the משנה a statement is attached to. The same words can sound unreasonable in one place and make perfect sense in another.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: They taught this only
when an animal tore it loose;
phrases.notes: This is about רבי ישמעאל's ruling that the halves make one impure by carrying.

phrases.english: but if a knife cut it loose, it is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא שנו אלא פלטתו חיה אבל פלטתו סכין בטיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual wording of רבי יוחנן's statement as taught on the סיפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אמי, רבי יוחנן said the half-כזיתים join only if an animal tore them loose. If a knife cut them loose, they are cancelled.

steps.title: Do you teach the rule only on the second case?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks רבי אמי if he applies רבי יוחנן's rule only to the סיפא. רבי אמי says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said to רבי אמי: Do you, Master, teach this rule on the latter clause? רבי אמי said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא checks that רבי אמי really puts רבי יוחנן's rule on the סיפא, the case of two half-כזיתים. רבי אמי confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, רב אושעיא saw רבי אמי apply the rule to the סיפא. Now he confirms this means the rule does not apply to the רישא, the case of one whole כזית. This sets up the contrast with עולא's version.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה; here, the case of two half-כזיתים
"Master"; a polite way to address a sage
Teaches / applies a teaching to
Yes

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אושעיא is speaking to רבי אמי.

phrases.english: Does the Master teach it on the latter clause?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the placement described in steps 31-32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אמי apply רבי יוחנן's rule only to the סיפא?

steps.title: Did עולא teach it on the first case?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי asks if עולא taught the rule on the רישא. רב אושעיא says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי asked: But did עולא say it to you on the first clause? רב אושעיא said: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי אמי asks a question back: did עולא really put the rule on the רישא, the case of a whole כזית? רב אושעיא says he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are clearly two versions of רבי יוחנן's rule. רבי אמי puts it on the סיפא. עולא put it on the רישא, and that version led to רב נחמן's sharp reaction in steps 28-29.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה; here, the case of one whole כזית of flesh
To you (plural)

phrases.english: But then, did עולא, on the first clause,
say it to you?
phrases.notes: "You" is plural: he means the sages in בבל who heard עולא.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question around to find out what עולא's version was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did עולא apply the rule to the רישא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, עולא taught it on the רישא.

steps.title: רבי אמי swears he would reject the first-case version
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says that if the rule is placed on the רישא, he would not accept it even from יהושע בן נון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By God, if יהושע בן נון himself told it to me, I would not listen to him!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי rejects עולא's version with an oath. He would not accept it even from יהושע בן נון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, רב נחמן was criticized for brushing off רבי יוחנן. Now it turns out that רב נחמן heard the rule placed on the רישא. In that form, רבי אמי agrees it cannot be right, and he even uses the same kind of oath רב נחמן used in step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: "By God"; a strong oath
I would not listen to him / accept it from him
From his own mouth

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי is not rejecting רבי יוחנן. He rejects only the version that puts the rule on the רישא. He still holds the rule is true on the סיפא.

phrases.english: He said to him: By God,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמַר לִי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ
phrases.english: if Yehoshua bin Nun told it to me from his own mouth,
I would not listen to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאֱלֹהִים אִי אָמַר לִי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing עולא's version, רבי אמי rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The version of רבי יוחנן's rule that applies it to the רישא (one whole כזית).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A whole כזית, and certainly bigger pieces, would not be cancelled just by being cut with a knife.

steps.title: רבין's group also taught it on the first case
steps.stepSummary: When רבין and the other sages came down from ארץ ישראל, they too taught רבי יוחנן's rule on the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין and all those who came down from ארץ ישראל arrived, they said it on the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new report. רבין and the other travelers from ארץ ישראל taught the rule on the רישא, just as עולא did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports עולא's version against רבי אמי's. Now many sages teach the rule on the רישא, so the גמרא cannot simply throw that version out.

keyTerms.meaning: "Those who go down": sages who traveled from ארץ ישראל to בבל and brought its teachings
They said it

phrases.english: When Ravin and all those who came down arrived,
they said it on the first clause.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין וְכׇל נָחוֹתֵי אַמְרוּהָ אַרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings new witnesses who agree with עולא, against רבי אמי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's rule (a piece cut loose with a knife is cancelled) was taught on the רישא, the case of a whole כזית.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes the רישא version the accepted one, so the גמרא now has to explain how it can make sense.

steps.title: Then the old problem returns
steps.stepSummary: If the rule is on the רישא, the difficulty comes back: would a knife cancel even a huge piece?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the problem with the רישא version. רב נחמן raised it, and רבי אמי rejected that version with an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If cutting with a knife cancels a whole כזית, the same logic would cancel a תרטא or a piece as big as a sifter (step 28). People would not really ignore such big pieces, so the rule seems unreasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty / problem
"But then"; brings out a problem that follows from what was just said

phrases.english: But then it is difficult!
phrases.notes: The difficulty is the one from steps 28-29: even a very large piece would be cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the problem that comes from accepting step 36's version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of רבי יוחנן's rule placed on the רישא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a knife cancels a כזית, it would also cancel very large pieces, which people would not ignore.

steps.title: The answer borrows a teaching of רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by pointing to something רב פפא said. The quote itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like what רב פפא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its answer. It will solve the problem using a teaching of רב פפא, which is quoted in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא borrows an idea that רב פפא said about a different matter. The details of that idea, and how it fixes the problem, come at the start of the next amud.

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the difficulty in step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Borrowing an idea from another sage's teaching (details still to come)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא version seems to cancel even huge pieces, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא's idea, quoted at the start of the next amud, will explain it.
